newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle rally late, end higher on covering.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle rally late, end higher on covering.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures staged a late short covering rally as general short covering touched off buy stops, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.950 to 0.250 cent per lb higher with August up 0.825 at 63.750 cents. Feeder cattle ended up 0.250 to unchanged with August up 0.100 at 80.100 cents.

Short covering and bottom hunting had provided support in live cattle futures from the start and demand increased late after the market held technical support. August traded above 63.000 cents much of the day despite closing under that level, a major technical point, on Tuesday, traders said.

The rally came despite the continued weak trend to both boxed beef and fed cattle markets. Further fund rolling added to strength in October which paced the rally. The "Goldman roll", Goldman Sachs commodity index fund's practice of rolling its long nearby positions into the next month for five trading days, had begun, sources said.

RBH, Refco, Lind-Waldock and Prudential Securities bought August. Refco also spread long October/short August along with Fimat Futures USA and Cargill Investor Services. In live cattle options, commission houses sold December 72 calls and Iowa Grains bought October 66 puts early, pit sources said.
Feeder cattle futures also rallied late on short covering sparked by the quick rally in live cattle. Some buy stops were also hit, traders said.
Demand in feeders came despite higher corn futures. An upturn in the latest CME feeder cattle index lent support early,sources said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.21 at $80.40 per cwt.
ADM Investor Services and mixed commission house demand was cited by traders late. Cargill Investor Services lightly spread long November feeders/short April live cattle, pit sources said.
Boneless beef and beef trimmings futures closed higher but under best levels. Further commercial buying boosted prices early before they ran into profit taking, traders said.
E.D.&F. Man bought August and October trimmings while buying in August boneless beef was considered speculative, pit sources said.

Boneless beef futures closed 0.50 cent per lb higher to unchanged with August of 0.20 at 95.80 cents. Trimmings ended 0.60 to 1.50 higher with August up the least at 46.00 cents. October and December boneless and all months of trimmings posted new contract highs.
